bc_cirque_of_the_unremarkables.blurb: A small ice and mixed venue in the Okanagan, north of Vernon, where the lines form right beside a road roundabout so there is essentially no walk. It has six climbs, all water ice: five at WI3 and one at WI4. A few of them carry a mixed section at the M3 to M4 level, and several can be set up as top-ropes, which makes it handy for a short day or for practising technique. Because the ice sits so close to the car, you can check how it is forming and be climbing within minutes. Expect a quick outing rather than a full day.

bc_mt_arrowsmith.blurb: Mt Arrowsmith is the high peak in the Alberni Valley region of central Vancouver Island, and it gives a mix of winter and rock objectives. It has six climbs: three ice and mixed routes between WI3 and WI4, two sport routes in the 5.10 to 5.12 range and one trad route at 5.11. The mountain is best known for ice and snow in winter. Low on the peak, a small ice pocket holds around half a dozen short lines of about 15 metres that suit beginners on top-rope when the ice is in, while longer mixed routes sit higher in the cirques.
